notes: Engine supplier for every Jolpica constructor-season, 1950 through 2026. constructorId is the Jolpica constructorId. One row is one engine used by that constructor in that season; several engines in one season are several rows. engine_name drops displacement and configuration tokens (for example 3.0 V8) and keeps the model. type works means that constructor's organization built the engine. type customer means an outside supplier on an ordinary supply, which is the default. type partner means a factory supply to a team that did not build the engine; the contract itself is not a column in the source table, so partner rows are medium confidence. type badged means the entered name is not the designer. Ford-Cosworth DFV and the later Ford-badged Cosworth programme names are not treated as badges: the supplier is Cosworth and the Ford name stays in engine_name. type unknown is used when the engine or the supplier was not established. confidence low means the make, the model, or the identity of the car is missing or in conflict. A missing notes field means the season table (or the Indianapolis 500 box score, for Indy-only constructors in 1950-1960) names this engine directly. Sources are English Wikipedia season pages, race pages, or Indianapolis 500 pages. This file does not copy Jolpica.

supply_types.meaning: The constructor's own organization built the engine.
An outside supplier, and not one of the factory-partner deals listed in the notes of those rows.
Factory supply to a team that did not build the engine. Judgment, medium confidence.
The name in the entry list is not the designer. badged_as holds the entered name.
Supplier or engine not established. confidence is low.
